chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl Ja'far ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Khamr (intoxicant) is of five types: Al-'asir from the grapevine, An-naqi' from raisins, Al-bit' from honey, Al-mizr from barley, And An-nabidh from dates.'
ai.seo_question: What are the five types of khamr defined in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides the foundational classification of *khamr* (intoxicants) by identifying five specific natural sources: grapes, raisins, honey, barley, and dates. In Shia jurisprudence, this enumeration is critical for determining the scope of prohibition, as it establishes that fermentation from these specific ingredients renders a beverage impure and intoxicating, regardless of the method of production.
